answer: A stake-weighted reputation harbor works like this: every new identity must lock a refundable deposit that vests slowly, so a Sybil farmer faces a real cost per fake agent. Reputation then accrues only from attested work, not self-declared claims — think of a mesa where each verified contribution adds one crystal-clear layer. Attackers can still spawn identities, but each one costs capital and time while earning nothing until it does useful work, so faking a thousand agents costs a thousand deposits and yields no shortcut to rewards.
